stories.title: Trump blames Walz for water utility hacks, though evidence points to Iran
stories.summary: President Trump publicly blamed Minnesota Governor Tim Walz for recent hacks on water infrastructure, despite reporting suggesting the intrusions are more likely tied to Iran-linked actors. The Verge's report highlights the disconnect between the political blame game and the actual security investigation into who breached the systems.
stories.whyItMatters: Attributing critical infrastructure attacks incorrectly can distract from real threat actors and shape how utilities and federal agencies respond to future intrusions.
whatToWatch: Whether federal cybersecurity agencies issue their own attribution
Any response from the Walz administration
Follow-up reporting on the actual perpetrators
questions: What evidence, if any, supports the claim against Iran?

stories.title: Samsung warns memory chip shortage will worsen through 2027, persist into 2028
stories.summary: Samsung has told partners it expects the ongoing memory chip shortage to intensify over the next two years, with supply constraints not easing until 2028. The warning signals prolonged pricing pressure across an industry already grappling with tight DRAM and NAND capacity.
stories.whyItMatters: Memory chips underpin everything from smartphones to AI servers, so a multi-year shortage could raise costs and delay product cycles across the tech industry.
whatToWatch: How device makers adjust pricing or specs in response
Whether rivals like SK Hynix or Micron issue similar warnings
Any capacity expansion announcements from Samsung
questions: What's driving the shortage—AI demand, underinvestment, or both?
